'''Glenn Alann ‘Tre’ Robinson III''' (born January 8, 1994) is an American professional [[basketball]] player for the [[Sharjah SC (basketball)|Sharjah SC]] of the [[UAE National Basketball League]]. He was drafted 40th overall by the [[Minnesota Timberwolves]] in the [[2014 NBA draft]]. He played nine seasons in the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA) for the Timberwolves, [[Philadelphia 76ers]], [[Indiana Pacers]], [[Detroit Pistons]], [[Golden State Warriors]] and [[Sacramento Kings]]. Robinson won the [[Slam Dunk Contest|NBA Slam Dunk Contest]] in 2017.

He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Michigan Wolverines men's basketball|Michigan Wolverines]], where he was an All-Freshman team honoree in during the [[2012–13 Big Ten Conference men's basketball season]] for the [[2012–13 Michigan Wolverines men's basketball team|2012–13 Michigan Wolverines team]] that finished as [[2013 NCAA Men's Division I Basketball Championship Game|national runner-up]] in the [[2013 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament]]. He returned to play for the [[2013–14 Big Ten Conference men's basketball season]] champion [[2013–14 Michigan Wolverines men's basketball team|2013–14 Wolverines]] before departing for the NBA.

Robinson was an all-state high school basketball player for [[Lake Central High School]] in [[St. John, Indiana]]. He is the son of [[Glenn Robinson]], the 1994 [[List of first overall NBA draft picks|first overall NBA draft pick]]. Two of his siblings were multiple time state champions in high school in individual events.

==Early life==
Robinson was prematurely born to his mother, Shantelle Clay, at Methodist Hospital in [[Gary, Indiana]].<ref name="GRIgis"/> He spent his first two months in an [[incubator (neonatal)|incubator]], until he was about {{convert|6|lb}}.<ref name="GRIgis">{{cite web |last=Rothstein |first=Michael |date=October 28, 2011 |title=Glenn Robinson III grows into star: Born prematurely and clinging to life, son of 'Big Dog' has blossomed into U-M commit |url=https://www.espn.com/colleges/michigan/basketball/story/_/id/7159849 |access-date=July 3, 2020 |publisher=[[ESPN]] |archive-date=July 4, 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200704095940/https://www.espn.com/colleges/michigan/basketball/story/_/id/7159849 |url-status=live }}</ref> He was raised by his mother and maternal grandmother.<ref name=GRIIFHOP/> By age three, he was a participant in the [[Hammond, Indiana]] [[YMCA]] children's basketball league.<ref name="GRIgis"/> At age 5 he played in a [[Boys & Girls Clubs of America]] basketball league.<ref name=GRIIFHOP/>

Growing up, Robinson had special NBA experiences. On January 2, 1998, when his father and [[Michael Jordan]] each scored 44 points against each other at the [[United Center]], he and his brother Gelen were in the front row.<ref name=GRIIFHOP/> When his father played for the [[Milwaukee Bucks]], Robinson remembers being kicked off the court by head coach [[George Karl]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.wbay.com/2023/11/08/nba-vet-glenn-robinson-iii-returns-basketball-joining-herd/|title=NBA vet Glenn Robinson III returns to basketball joining the Herd|accessdate=March 30, 2024|date=November 7, 2023|work=[[WBAY]]|author=Torres, Adriana|archive-date=March 30, 2024|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240330202000/https://www.wbay.com/2023/11/08/nba-vet-glenn-robinson-iii-returns-basketball-joining-herd/|url-status=live}}</ref> During a meeting in the [[Philadelphia 76ers]] locker room with [[Allen Iverson]], Iverson referred to him as "Shorty", and the younger Robinson noted that he was as tall as Iverson, saying "Man, I’m your height right now! Who are you calling shorty?"<ref name=GRIIFHOP>{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/kings/blog/glenn-robinson-iii-forging-his-own-path-0|title=Glenn Robinson III Is Forging His Own Path|accessdate=March 30, 2024|date=January 29, 2021|work=[[NBA.com]]|author=Kramers, Alex|archive-date=March 30, 2024|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240330193245/https://www.nba.com/kings/blog/glenn-robinson-iii-forging-his-own-path-0|url-status=live}}</ref>

Robinson attended Grimmer Middle School in [[Schererville, Indiana]] prior to attending [[Lake Central High School]] in [[St. John, Indiana]].<ref name="Bbpoty"/> He stood at {{convert|5|ft|6|in}} in seventh grade and {{convert|6|ft|1|in}} two years later as a freshman.<ref name="GRIgis"/> Robinson was nearly {{convert|6|ft|4|in}} during his sophomore season and stood at more than {{convert|6|ft|5.5|in|2}} as a junior.<ref name="GRIbtfsoaNptctMb"/>

==High school career==
As a freshman, he played [[junior varsity]] for Lake Central.<ref name="LWiC"/> At the time, his father lived in Atlanta, and Robinson grew up with his mother, Shantelle Clay-Irving alongside his younger brother Gelen.<ref name="LWiC"/> During the summer between his freshman and sophomore season, he came under the wing of two substitute father figures: Dave Milausnic, Lake Central Varsity Basketball head coach, and Wayne Brumm, AAU SYF Players under-17 coach.<ref name="LWiC"/> Milausnic convinced Robinson to come to the gym for early morning workouts, often waking Robinson at his home.<ref name="LWiC"/> Brumm, who would continue to mentor Robinson as a collegian, advised him to hire a personal trainer named Andrew Wallen, who helped Robinson augment his [[vertical leap]]. He also helped Robinson bulk up from {{convert|167|lb}} prior to his sophomore year to {{convert|210|lb}} in two years.<ref name="LWiC"/>

==Personal life==
Robinson is the founder of the Angels are Real Indeed, Foundation,<ref>{{Cite web|title=About - ARI Foundation|url=https://arifoundation.org/about/|access-date=2021-02-19|language=en-US|archive-date=January 23, 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210123034620/https://arifoundation.org/about/|url-status=live}}</ref> a nonprofit organization dedicated to providing resources to fatherless families. Based in his hometown of [[Gary, Indiana]], the ARI Foundation is named after Robinson's daughter, Ariana. The ARI Foundation has hosted toy drives, back-to-school supply and holiday-specific fundraisers, and has furnished the apartments of working-class single mothers.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Welcoming Lynn's Angel - ARI Foundation|url=https://arifoundation.org/blog/welcoming-lynns-angel/|access-date=2021-02-19|language=en-US|archive-date=January 23, 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210123044417/https://arifoundation.org/blog/welcoming-lynns-angel/|url-status=live}}</ref> The nonprofit's work has been featured in [[CNN]],<ref>{{Cite web |last1=York |first1=Jeff |last2=Davies |first2=Amanda |name-list-style=and |title=NBA star on life inside the NBA 'bubble' and fighting for social justice |url=https://edition.cnn.com/2020/08/13/sport/nba-glenn-robinson-iii-social-justice-fatherhood-spt-intl/index.html |access-date=2021-02-19 |website=CNN|date=August 13, 2020 }}</ref> [[Sports Illustrated]]<ref>{{Cite web|last=Grasso|first=Justin|title=Glenn Robinson III Plans to Donate for Every Point he Scores|url=https://www.si.com/nba/76ers/news/76ers-glenn-robinson-iii-donate-point-scores|access-date=2021-02-19|website=Sports Illustrated|date=June 30, 2020|language=en|archive-date=July 1, 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200701212211/https://www.si.com/nba/76ers/news/76ers-glenn-robinson-iii-donate-point-scores|url-status=live}}</ref> and [[USA Today]].<ref>{{Cite web|date=2020-06-05|title=INTERVIEW: Glenn Robinson III raising money with ARI Foundation to fight racial injustice|url=https://sixerswire.usatoday.com/2020/06/05/interview-glenn-robinson-iii-raising-money-with-ari-foundation-to-fight-racial-injustice/|access-date=2021-02-19|website=Sixers Wire|language=en-US|archive-date=January 28, 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210128155142/https://sixerswire.usatoday.com/2020/06/05/interview-glenn-robinson-iii-raising-money-with-ari-foundation-to-fight-racial-injustice/|url-status=live}}</ref>
